app_review_notes:
MOVIE MODE is a local iPhone video recorder and editor. No login or subscription is required.

Tap + on Movies to create a movie and open the camera immediately. Allow Camera and Microphone access to record a clip. Tap the red button to start/stop. Tap the recent-clip thumbnail to review/edit; Watch Movie plays the assembled movie. The clip editor's Done saves edits. Its three-dot menu includes Save Edited Clip to Photos. Export Movie creates a finished copy for Photos, Files, or sharing. Photos permission is add-only and requested when saving.

Recording defaults to Standard. Before the first clip, open the camera gear > Recording Settings to choose Apple Log on supported hardware. In Log, the look button opens Look & Preview for Natural, Cinema, or imported looks. The camera Viewfinder choices are With Look, Log, and False Color; playback offers With Look and Log. These preview choices do not change the recorded originals. Import Look asks for the LUT creator's input format (Apple Log or Rec.709) before choosing a .cube file.

The PiP camera button opens Picture in Picture before recording, with an on/off switch, live preview, and Inset, Top & Bottom, or Side by Side layouts. During a prepared dual-camera recording, the button toggles PiP immediately. Apple Log, simultaneous front/rear PiP, zoom ranges, and camera switching depend on hardware and recording configuration.

Dolly opens Start/End controls: select a point, choose a lens, and press Go. End scrubbing temporarily previews that framing and returns to Start on release. The delay applies only to Dolly movement, not the recording start. Dolly Settings and How to Use Dolly are available from the camera gear.

The Movies gear opens app Settings. Storage contains Recently Deleted. Backup & Recovery contains project backups, optional original-clip copies to Photos, and recording recovery. Help & Support contains contact information, permissions, and Diagnostics. Settings > Privacy includes the public privacy policy. Projects and diagnostics stay local unless the user saves/shares them. Recently Deleted supports restore or permanent deletion; external Photos/Files copies remain separate.
